findings.problem: Both READMEs present the 30-day retention of YouTube API items as something the skill does. README.ko.md says the items are deleted after the deadline ('기한이 지나면 지웁니다'); README.md says 'Items from the API are kept 30 days (`retention_until`)'. Nothing deletes or refuses an expired item. `retention_until` is only stamped on the result, printed in the envelope header and written to the ledger. The bundle validator has no check for it (the bundle contract lists that check as planned). The only timed deletion is the reader's own page text (72 h, or at `close`). Excerpts, bundles and reports made from API items are left to the agent and the user. This is the one legal-exposure promise (YouTube developer policy) in the READMEs that the code does not keep.
findings.evidence: README.md:151 and README.ko.md:96. `grep -n retention uxresearch/*.py scripts/*.py` shows stamping and printing only (cli.py:84-85, ladder.py:776, youtube.py:498-618), no deletion and no expiry check. scripts/validate_bundle.py never reads retention_until. references/research/evidence-bundle-contract.md:96-104 (both copies) says 'will add these checks (planned)' for an official_api source's retention_until. ledger.py:76 PAGE_TTL_S = 72 h and Run.close() removing pages/ are the only purges. The code lane's own note says: 'retention_until is stamped but not enforced downstream; the gate or validator that drops excerpts after 30 days is deferred'. The docs elsewhere (public-page-access.md:570-572 and 821-822, research/workflow.md:243) correctly word it as a duty: 'Delete them, or read them again, by then'.
findings.fix: Reword both READMEs to separate what is enforced from what is a duty, for example: 'The reader stamps each API item with retention_until (fetch time + 30 days) and deletes its own page text at close or after 72 h. You and the agent must delete excerpts, bundles and reports built from API items by that date; the planned gate will refuse expired items.' Keep the Korean text in step. Optionally have `close` print the earliest retention_until it saw so the duty is visible.

findings.problem: The change grows references/ from 256,655 B to 705,919 B (2.75x) and creates six files over 40 KB where there were none: platform-map.md 102,653 B (898 lines), legal-checklist.md 81,889 B (814), public-page-access.md 58,819 B (889; was 35,267 B), promotion.md 50,262 B (383), kwcag-2.2.md 45,630 B (279), statistics.md 42,426 B (293). The Korean pack is 385,785 B in eight files. An agent is unlikely to read the two largest fully: platform-map.md has about 62k characters of which 19.8k are Hangul, roughly 30-40k tokens by estimate, and legal-checklist.md roughly 25-30k, both above a typical 25k-token single read, so the agent must page or grep. Nothing tells it to read by section. overview.md's stage table sends A0 to legal-checklist.md as 'first file to read' although the A0 material is the 15-line table in its section 6 (lines 751-766); A1 sends it to platform-map.md and statistics.md without a section hint. Also, uxresearch/data/korea-platforms.json (127,217 B) and korea-statistics.json (108,790 B) ship in the installed folder, are described as the 'source' of platform-map.md and statistics.md, and are opened only by tests: no runtime code reads them. An agent that takes 'source' literally loads another ~70k tokens.
findings.evidence: `git ls-tree -r -l 877058b/b0b04bf skills/remorsearch-ux-qa/references` gives 256,655 B and 705,919 B, and 0 versus 6 files over 40 KB. findings.fix: (1) overview.md A0 row: point to legal-checklist.md section 6 (and the section 3 table) instead of the file. (2) Add a two-line reading guide at the top of platform-map.md, legal-checklist.md, promotion.md, statistics.md and kwcag-2.2.md: which sections every run reads and which are lookups by channel or row ID. findings.problem: The docs describe `access_policy.render: driver` as 'the bundled page reader, drivers/web/read_page.mjs'. The reader does not run it. With `driver` set, `read` still ends `unread` with R3 untried and prints the note 'the render driver is not available in this version; use the host browser and ingest'. public-page-access.md section 4 says the reader never starts a browser itself. So one of the three brief values is documented as working and behaves like `host_browser` plus a warning.
findings.evidence: audience-pipeline.md:141-142; schemas/ux-research-brief.v1.schema.json:96-97 ('the web driver'); uxresearch/ladder.py:652-654 (`if render == 'driver': notes.append('the render driver is not available in this version; use the host browser and ingest')`). Reproduced: `ux_research.py start --run R --render driver`, then `read` of a JS-shell fixture page returns exit 4, `untried: ['R3']`, `notes: ['the render driver is not available in this version; use the host browser and ingest']`, `render: 'needs_host_render'`. findings.fix: Document `driver` as reserved (behaves like host_browser, adds a note), or remove it from the enum in ledger.RENDER_MODES, the schema, `start --render` and audience-pipeline.md. If the intent is 'the agent may run read_page.mjs', say that under `host_browser`.

findings.problem: The install docs and the capability table never say the Python tools need a POSIX system. uxresearch/ledger.py and uxloop/storage.py import `fcntl` at module load, so on Windows `ux_research.py` (even `--help`) and `ux_loop.py` fail before doing anything. The only statement of the limit is repo-root requirements.txt ('Linux/macOS (POSIX flock)'), which is not in the installable folder and is not linked from either README or SKILL.md. The new 'Needs' column lists Node, Playwright, a YouTube key and a write grant, but not the operating system.
findings.evidence: uxresearch/ledger.py:43 `import fcntl`, :479 `fcntl.flock`; uxloop/storage.py:4 and :26. Simulated on this Linux box with `sys.modules['fcntl'] = None` then running scripts/ux_research.py --help: `ModuleNotFoundError: import of fcntl halted; None in sys.modules`. README.md:36-37 says only 'Python tools (3.10+, standard library only)'; README.md:17-22 table has no OS entry; SKILL.md:109 says 'Python 3.10+ standard library only'. requirements.txt:2 holds the POSIX note. Python 3.10 and 3.13 both run the reader from the copied folder.
findings.fix: Add 'Linux or macOS (WSL on Windows); the reader and loop use POSIX file locks' to the README Install section, both language versions, and to SKILL.md's Tools paragraph. Or replace fcntl with a portable lock so the statement is not needed.

summary: 16 findings: 0 blocker, 2 major, 14 minor. Docs and code are closely aligned; the problems are a README promise the code does not keep, the size and navigation of the new Korean pack, and packaging hygiene.
